First, let's simplify the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}^{2}-16 & >9 \\ 5{x}^{2} & >9+16 \\ 5{x}^{2} & >25 \\ {x}^{2} & >5\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use either of two methods to solve the inequality.

*Method 1 - Solving an Absolute Value Equation*

Taking the square root of both sides of the inequality, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{x}^{2}} & >\sqrt{5} \\ |x| & >\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the definition of absolute value, we must have 

$$
x<-\sqrt{5}\,\text{or}\,x>\sqrt{5}.
$$

So, the solution is $x\in (-\infty ,-\sqrt{5})\cup (\sqrt{5},+\infty ).$

*Method 2 - Picturing a Quadratic Curve*

Starting from ${x}^{2}>5$ and moving all terms to the left-hand side, we reach

$$
{x}^{2}-5>0.
$$

Now, we consider the corresponding parabola given by $\,y={x}^{2}-5\,$ and find its roots:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-5 & >0 \\ {x}^{2}-{(\sqrt{5})}^{2} & =0 \\ (x-\sqrt{5})(x+\sqrt{5}) & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

hence $x=\pm \sqrt{5}.$

Since the leading coefficient of ${x}^{2}-5$   is positive, the parabola  opens upward.  Therefore, the solution set to the  given inequality ($y>0$) lies outside the roots (but does not include them):

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13965374/assets/52b970419b3dbb9498e6b7b05d031195b1e8fae9bdba0428dd72f84f0101095b.png)

 

Therefore, the solution is $x\in (-\infty ,-\sqrt{5})\cup (\sqrt{5},\infty ).$
